A prior live guest displayed Golden Gate wallpaper, a Finder window, the Dock, and calendar/weather widget content. App icons and some glass effects remain corrupted; guest GPU restart attempts are recorded.

The newer heap/native-format renderer candidate built successfully but its live boot currently shows a black display; private-plane query refusals and guest fence waits are recorded.
A private comparison clearing the unsupported Apple feature profile draws a transitional login wallpaper without the former private-plane query refusals; full desktop verification remains pending.

The private capability comparison authenticated and displayed wallpaper, widgets, Finder menus, and Dock placeholders. Every app icon is not yet correct, and a Finder window was not verified in this comparison.

The capability comparison later panicked with a guest allocation modified after free, following repeated GPU resets. Four Vulkan validation errors reported nonzero-offset sampling with pixel-coordinate samplers; investigation and live verification remain pending.

The last diagnostic boot, using an earlier revision, resolves every submitted object-table entry and reads 161 compact execute packets and one compact info packet without framing errors. Guest-write and guest-invalidation flags are present. Execution and query replies remain refused, so the display stays black. No guest panic, GPU restart or Vulkan validation error was observed before the diagnostic VM was stopped; this does not establish desktop acceptance.

contracts: Failed surface and GVA transfers retain the same debt, age, native identity and content for retry.
A failed transfer does not advance the guest-write witness.
Named synchronization reports the first unfinished resource. Successful earlier transfers are not repeated.
Both synchronization opcodes retain their parked position on failure; no completion stamp or discard occurs until successful transfer submission.
The existing GPU completion owner orders submitted writes before visible completion; submission alone is not completion.
Texture gathering, compute staging, blits, mapped guest reads and writes, and scanout refuse access through failed required transfers.
Retired or superseded surface debts release their original resident without writing into replacement backing.
regressions: Before-fix failure changes the guest-write stamp and loses its debt.

A parked synchronization packet leaves its completion stamp unchanged across retries, then publishes after pixels transfer successfully.
Synchronize-and-discard preserves transfer backing during failure and discards after successful submission.
Unpaid guest reads leave destination bytes unchanged, and refused overwrites preserve guest memory.
Older gather and writer tests incorrectly treated discarded debt without a native image as successful payment; they now assert refusal and retained debt.

compact_gpu_execution.scope: Compact Execute 0x43 admission and retained preparation/execution/synchronization on Linux/Vulkan. Shared buffers, private single-sample 2D color textures (ordinary or generated mipmaps), and mapper textures are supported resource families; other families refuse before admission. Bazel assembly, source reproduction and artifact privacy verified; live desktop verification is pending.
contracts: All command streams and resource identities are retained before admission; compact and legacy retained inputs cannot be interchanged or supplied together.
Whole-resource dependencies order preparation even when a resource is not referenced by a command.
Flag bit 0 consumes guest-write declarations across the complete list before preparation; bit 1 applies after every resource prepares; bit 2 requests post-execution synchronization.
Shared buffers retain physical pages; ordinary paged textures upload missing levels and generated textures generate native mipmaps; mapper construction registers its retained mapping.
Shared buffers and mapper textures remain guest-valid; prepared paged consumers use the native content owner rather than a guest-valid cache.
Failed preparation retains its phase and index; completed guest-write declarations do not replay.
Commands execute once; failed synchronization retains its unfinished resource index and skips the completed prefix on retry.
Resources stay retained through Vulkan fences; completion uses the existing GPU-ordered publication owner.
Nested transfer refusals preserve their canonical diagnostic owner instead of registering duplicate identifiers.
regressions: Both page geometries: forced preparation and synchronization failures withhold completion stamps; retained inputs survive modified command bytes and remapped/unmapped buffer pages.
A native image made ready between preparation attempts is not invalidated by replaying an earlier guest-write declaration.
A buffer fill executes once, completed texture synchronization does not repeat, and the final texture readback precedes completion publication.
A bad later command stream and an unsupported resource family cause no preparation, command write or acknowledgement.
Admission refuses missing, mismatched or duplicate legacy/compact retained inputs.
Full device testing exposed a diagnostic-owner collision, now fixed in both compact and paged wrappers.

reference_branch_comparison.scope: Read-only comparison of remote-verified main/master against the built 122-path local checkpoint; paused decoder draft excluded.
reference_branch_comparison.core_boot_patches: All 135 target/arm, 40 accel/tcg and 35 system files match both references. vmapple.c differs in graphics transport selection, not Golden Gate boot logic.
reference_branch_comparison.master_qrm_fixes: Present: dynamic texel widths/whole-run bounds, snapshot format-width checks, scalar descriptor completeness, native readback/layout-checked stores, quiet stale probes and typed non-view handling.
reference_branch_comparison.translator: Both reference translator trees match each other. Local runtime changes add aggregate sampler sidecar preservation; no missing reference runtime translator change identified.
reference_branch_comparison.confirmed_regression: USB HID logical/usage maximum is 101 locally versus 255 in both reference branches. Extended keys may be lost; this does not explain the black boot.
reference_branch_comparison.platform_gap: Reference Windows shim packs scattered RAM aliases and advertises stable mappings; local Linux MMIO shim supports direct contiguous mappings and rejects fragmented aliases. Buffer copying/caching can differ. Vulkan RAMBlock imports are a separate path; no blanket claim that all GPU imports are disabled.
reference_branch_comparison.protocol_gap: Both references cap protocol at 62 and retain the same narrow mapper decoder as the built local checkpoint. Local negotiation selects 237, exposing Descriptor2/compact paths. The black boot reports impossible mapper width; an authored wide 1920x1080 descriptor reproduces it. The subsequent private decoder draft is unverified.
reference_branch_comparison.launch_difference: Reference active launcher uses one ARM vCPU and shared RAM; local defaults use four vCPUs and normal RAM. Both use 8 GiB, cpu=max, TCG, the same verbose boot arguments and writeback disk caching. No timing benchmark performed.
reference_branch_comparison.intentional_exclusions: Windows-only hash-locked Lavapipe DLL patch, proprietary AIR fixtures and account-specific auto-login helpers are absent from the public Linux project.
reference_branch_comparison.reference_acceptance: Both reference handoffs describe Finder/Dock acceptance as incomplete; neither is a verified full-desktop baseline.
reference_branch_comparison.next_priority: Complete/verify the Descriptor2 mapper decoder, then use a matched one-vCPU control to separate protocol failures from CPU/copy throughput. Restore the keyboard range separately.
